hook.say: What if you built a ladder all the way to space... and started climbing?

lines.goal: Space starts sixty-two miles straight up. No rocket. Just rungs.
lines.tower: Half an hour in, you pass the tallest building on Earth... and you've barely started.
lines.sunrise: Keep climbing. Above the clouds, the sun comes up early, while the city below is still asleep.
lines.halfair: Your ears pop. Half of all the air on Earth is now below your boots.
lines.everest: You're higher than Everest. Without the suit, you'd black out in about a minute.
lines.plane: A jet slides past at eye level. Inside, people are eating pretzels. Out here, it's seventy below.
lines.armstrong: At sixty-two thousand feet, the air is so thin that your spit would boil.
lines.skydive: This is where the highest skydive in history began. And you're not even halfway.

black.say: The sky turns black... in the middle of the day.

lines.meteors: Shooting stars burn up all around you, in the coldest air on the planet.
lines.tail: Here's the catch. Let go, and you fall straight back down. To stay up here, you'd need to fly seventeen thousand miles an hour... sideways.

outro.say: Space is only an hour's drive away... if your car could go straight up.
